sermon.title: The Simplicity That is in Christ
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: From 2 Corinthians 11:3 Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that Christ is simple and that his church grows morally even in corrupt nations. Walking through Rome, the mistreatment of Jews, Israel’s 1948 survival and America’s flaws, he says people are still drawn to what is good, and from Ecclesiastes, Deuteronomy, Genesis 1 and Isaiah 9 shows that wisdom excels folly and believers reflect Jesus, the great light.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: At 17:30 he cites “Jude 1:25” for “the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only wise God”; that wording is 1 Timothy 1:17 (linked). He first says “Psalm 74:6” and then correctly “Psalm 74:16.” Historical figures and statistics are as spoken and unchecked (six million Jews plus seven million others; 30 million Arabs vs 650,000 Jews; $5,000 planes vs $170,000; about 30,000 yearly deaths from STDs; 1,600 children killed and 600,000 abused yearly; a candle seen 30 miles). Sensitive content kept as spoken: Islam called sectarian and bigoted (with Bush/Obama named), Hillary Clinton and the Democratic debate, Catholic priests abusing children, Truman’s embargo.

faqs.question: Why does he stress “may have peace” in John 16:33?
faqs.answer: Because it is your decision whether you accept and follow him; peace takes a commitment, but trouble in the world is certain.

faqs.question: What does simplicity mean here?
faqs.answer: Nothing complicated—when people complicate Jesus or the Bible it is a sign they don’t know them.

faqs.question: Is abortion new?
faqs.answer: No—he says in the Roman Empire women would throw a delivered child in a river or use chemicals to abort.

faqs.question: Who besides Jews died in the Nazi camps, according to the sermon?
faqs.answer: He says about seven million others, mostly Slavs—Czechoslovakians, Poles and Russians—whom Hitler declared inferior.

faqs.question: Did America help Israel in 1948?
faqs.answer: He says America accepted them as a nation but did not help, and Truman’s embargo blocked arms sales.

faqs.question: Does the church force people to join or stay?
faqs.answer: No—he says no one is physically forcing them to join or forbidding them to leave, unlike Muslims and other religions.

faqs.question: Should Christians refuse to judge?
faqs.answer: He says “don’t judge” is foolish; keeping God’s rules and making judgments is our wisdom before the nations.

faqs.question: Is drunkenness serious?
faqs.answer: He says the Bible calls drunkenness a hell sin, and says not even to look on the wine when it is red in the cup.

faqs.question: Does he call forced redistribution stealing?
faqs.answer: He says taking something from someone without their permission is stealing, and applies it to promises of making the rich pay for everything.

faqs.question: Were the creation days long ages?
faqs.answer: He says the evening and the morning were the first day as the earth rotated, and God repeats that he made heaven and earth in six days.
